classification.difficultyReason: Read equally spaced ordinates from diagrams and substitute into the trapezoidal rule.

content.prompt: Use the trapezoidal rule to find the approximate area of each irregular figure.

spec.description: Unshaded irregular region with black arrowed axes and blue boundary and ordinates. Horizontal ticks are 1, 2 and 3; horizontal units are absent from the source.
spec.mathematics: Equally spaced ordinates at x=0,1,2,3 have lengths 2.9 km, 2.3 km, 2.1 km and 3.2 km. The unspecified upper boundary decreases to a trough between 1 and 2, then rises.
spec.answerVisibility: All ordinate measurements are permanent givens; no answer is shown.

answer.short: $A\approx7.45\text{ km}^2$, assuming the horizontal coordinates are in kilometres.
answer.worked:
Taking the horizontal coordinates in kilometres, $h=1\text{ km}$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&\approx\frac{1}{2}\bigl[2.9+3.2+2(2.3+2.1)\bigr]\\&=\frac{1}{2}(14.9)\\&=7.45\text{ km}^2.\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Unshaded irregular region with black arrowed axes and blue boundary and ordinates. Horizontal ticks are 1, 2, 3 and 4; horizontal units are absent from the source.
spec.mathematics: Equally spaced ordinates at x=0,1,2,3,4 have lengths 9.8 m, 11.3 m, 9.1 m, 9.7 m and 8.5 m. The unspecified boundary peaks near 1, dips near 2 and rises near 3 before falling to 4.
spec.answerVisibility: All ordinate measurements are permanent givens; no answer is shown.

answer.short: $A\approx39.25\text{ m}^2$, assuming the horizontal coordinates are in metres.
answer.worked:
Taking the horizontal coordinates in metres, $h=1\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&\approx\frac{1}{2}\bigl[9.8+8.5+2(11.3+9.1+9.7)\bigr]\\&=\frac{1}{2}(78.5)\\&=39.25\text{ m}^2.\end{aligned}$$
